item.title: Weekly Newsletter #24 — May 7, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #24 · May 07, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 NEXT THURSDAY: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Our book talk event with Life After Cars authors Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon is next week!

Life After Cars Book Event
with Sarah Goodyear & Doug Gordon from The War on Cars Podcast
NEXT THURSDAY, May 14th at 7 PM
Resurrection Philadelphia, 17th & Sansom Streets

Get Your Ticket Today

 
The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion, State Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

Get Your Ticket Today

🚲 BIKE TO WORK AND WHEREVER DAY

Next Wednesday, May 13th, is Bike to Work and Wherever Day!

Celebrate biking as transport by riding with a bike train from one of five locations throughout the city to City Hall for a press conference emphasizing the need for Vision Zero & creating safer streets for bicyclists and pedestrians.

📢 SUPPORT A SAFER ARAMINGO AVE

Tell PennDOT to make Aramingo Ave safer!
Glenn Colville was killed while riding his bike on Aramingo Avenue by a driver who plowed through plastic flexposts into the bike lane.
Aramingo has been on Philly's High-Injury Network for nearly a decade--it's time PennDOT makes it safer by:
  1. Replacing plastic flex posts with concrete protection 
  2. Providing funding so the City of Philadelphia can complete its Aramingo Avenue Traffic Safety project

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

Take this quick, 3-minute survey to help the Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails understand how you use trails throughout the region.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

May 13

Bike to Work and Wherever Day

7:50 AM meet, 8:00 AM roll · Various Locations

Celebrate biking as transport with a ride from one of five locations throughout the city to City Hall, followed by a press conference emphasizing the need for Vision Zero & creating safer streets for bicyclists and pedestrians.
May 14

Life After Cars Book Talk

7:00 PM, doors open 6:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S. 17th St

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
May 20

2026 Ride of Silence

6:45 PM · North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum steps

Honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets with a ride in complete silence throughout the city. The ride will cover 8 miles at a slow, casual pace and will occur rain or shine.
May 30

Hunting Park Hustle

9:00 AM to 2:00 PM · Hunting Park

Hunting Park goes car-free for a day full of biking and running events.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

The Philadelphia Tribune / Councilmember Young pushes back on critics of senior housing in North Philadelphia

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

The Philadelphia Citizen / Ideas We Should Steal: Fix the Sidewalks!

Inquirer.com / These Manayunk public stairs have been closed for 13 years. A civic group wants them fixed and reopened.

Inquirer.com / Head House Square’s restoration has begun with a $1.5 million makeover

Grid Magazine / Cyclist maps bike path from 30th Street to Atlantic City - Grid Magazine

🚌 TRANSIT

PhillyVoice / City Council to consider expanding SEPTA’s student fare program

Billy Penn at WHYY / Philly travelers cheer reopening of intercity bus station, mostly

🚲 MOBILITY

Axios / Philly traffic deaths drop as state hits historic low

Inquirer.com / The city changed the direction of a Kensington street, but not everyone is following the new flow

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Sightline Institute / Lead Researcher, Housing and Cities

Philadelphia Housing Authority / Planning and Development Manager

University City District / Senior Vice President of Finance and Administration

Pa Senate Democratic Caucus / Organizing and Advocacy Director

DVRPC

  • Community Planner
  • Operations & Organizational Development Intern

Delaware County / Open Space & Trails Planner

Commonwealth of Pennsylvania / Enterprise Solutions Director (Information Technology Executive 3)

Pennsylvania Horticultural Society

  • Senior Manager, Social Media & Engagement

  • Integrated Marketing Program Manager

  • Temporary Campaign Manager

City of Philadelphia

  • Senior Capital Project Manager, Roosevelt Boulevard
  • Lead GIS Analyst
  • Transportation Grants Coordinator
  • Policy and Analysis Intern
  • Art and Design Intern
  • Citizens Planning Institute Intern
  • Historical Preservation Intern
  • Watershed and Development Research Intern

PA Stands Up / 2026 Field Organizers

Fair Share Housing Center / Staff Attorney

Art Reach / Communications Manager

 

Do You Like This Newsletter and Our Advocacy Work?

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

Join Us as a Member TODAY

 

5th Square Advocacy is a grassroots nonprofit organization driven to advance a vision for a more accessible, sustainable, equitable Philadelphia for all residents. Donations are not tax deductible.

Website Instagram Become a Member Volunteer

Weekly Newsletter #23 · April 30, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏛️ SUPPORT A BUDGET THAT KEEPS PHILLY MOVING

Next Wednesday at 10am, come to City Hall to speak in support of our transportation budget priorities.

FY27 City Council Budget Hearings - Public Comment
Philadelphia City Council Chambers, City Hall, Room 400
Wednesday, May 6th, 10am

See here for more details about how to sign up, and resources to help you craft your testimony.

You can also help by taking City Council's city budget survey.

📚 TWO WEEKS: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Get your tickets before they sell out!

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
 
Get Your Ticket Today

🚏 NEW BUS TERMINAL NOW OPEN

We were thrilled to attend the opening of the newly-renovated intercity bus terminal! After years of advocacy working with Transit Forward Philadelphia, we celebrate the city finally treating bus riders with dignity.

🏫 STUDENTS DESERVE BETTER TRANSIT ACCESS

Current student fare cards don't do enough to meet the needs of Philadelphia's students--sign this petition to give them the transit access they deserve!

We need students fare cards that expand coverage to evenings, weekends, and summers, and are given to all students regardless of where in the city they live.

🚲 $1 INDEGO PASSES

To celebrate Bike Month, Indego is offering $1 monthly passes with promo code INDEPRO26.

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

The Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails want to know your thoughts about trails in the Greater Philadelphia and southern New Jersey region and how you use them.

Take their quick, 3-minute survey here!

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Billy Penn at WHYY / Philadelphia aims to expand delivery loading zones

“Just the past few years, e-commerce and food-ordering businesses have exploded in popularity and caused tremendous stress in our roads and along our curbs,” testified Miles Owen, co-chair of the 5th Square Advocacy urbanist group. “These bills are absolutely necessary and smart policy to modernize the use of curb space in our city to make roads safer.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Apr 30

Parking Protected Bike Lane & Pedestrian Safety Advocacy Call

6:00 PM to 7:00 PM · Virtual via Zoom

Join Bicycle Coalition Policy Director Julio Rodriguez for a virtual call about Parking Protected Bike Lanes (PPB), Jay Alert Pilot, Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA), and their upcoming June 9 advocacy day in Harrisburg.
May 02

John Heinz Bike Tour

2:00 PM to 3:00 PM · John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge

Join Ranger Ben for a Bike Tour around John Heinz NWR! Bring your own bike for this 4-5 mile ride on gravel trails. Register with Ben at benjamin_breslau@fws.gov.
May 14

Life After Cars Book Talk

7:00 PM, doors open 6:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S. 17th St

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
May 20

2026 Ride of Silence

6:45 PM · North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum steps

Honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets with a ride in complete silence throughout the city. The ride will cover 8 miles at a slow, casual pace and will occur rain or shine.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

WHYY / New apartments planned for Germantown parcel with history of illegal dumping

remappingdebate.org / Revolving loan funds: The hottest trend in housing finance

The Philadelphia Citizen / Will PA’s Housing Reform Plans Exclude Philly?

🚲 MOBILITY

Billy Penn at WHYY / Philadelphia aims to expand delivery loading zones

FOX 29 Philadelphia / Fishtown neighbors call for safer Girard Avenue after drivers use trolley lane to pass

  • Operations & Organizational Development Intern

  • Integrated Marketing Program Manager

  • Temporary Campaign Manager

  • Marketing Intern

City of Philadelphia

  • Senior Capital Project Manager, Roosevelt Boulevard
  • Lead GIS Analyst
  • Transportation Grants Coordinator
  • Policy and Analysis Intern
  • Art and Design Intern
  • Citizens Planning Institute Intern
  • Historical Preservation Intern
  • Watershed and Development Research Intern

item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #22 · April 23, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 NEXT MONTH: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Get your tickets before they sell out!

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
 
Get Your Ticket Today

🕯️ RIDE OF SILENCE

Each year, Philadelphia's bicyclists come together to remember and honor those on bikes who were killed or injured by motorists with a ride around the city in complete silence. Since last year's ride, 13 bicyclists have been killed in the Delaware Valley.

This year's Ride of Silence will happen next month on May 20th. Following a brief ceremony at 6:45pm at the north apron of City Hall, participants will bike at a casual pace around the city ending at the Art Museum steps.

🚏 NEW BUS TERMINAL OPENS NEXT WEEK

Next week, the former Greyhound bus terminal will be reopening as a freshly renovated hub for Philadelphia's intercity bus passengers.

 

Check out this article from the Inquirer for a sneak peek: See inside the new Greyhound Terminal on Filbert Street

Ever since the terminal first closed years ago, we've been fighting for a facility that meets the needs of our city's bus riders so we're very excited for it to open next week!

🥳 SATURDAY: CELEBRATE TRAILS DAY

This Saturday, April 25th, is Celebrate Trails Day!

We have a great network of trails throughout the region--so let's celebrate them!

There will be outdoor community events throughout the city and region at various times throughout the day. Find an event here.

 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Philadelphia Tribune / Philly residents show up to Council Chambers, testify overwhelmingly for mayor’s proposed taxes

Jerrett Johnson of 5th Square, a transit advocacy group, urged the Council to approve a new delivery fee for nonessential products, saying the tax “will allocate funds for public transportation without impacting schools.”

Billy Penn at WHYY / Free, year-round SEPTA passes proposed for all Philly students

The passes work from 5:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. on school days, but are deactivated overnight and on weekends, holidays and over the summer. 

Transit advocate Will Tung held up his daughter’s pass during a City Hall press conference Monday and compared it to Cinderella’s carriage, which “turns into a pumpkin, useless,” at midnight.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

 

🚌 KEEP TRANSIT WINS IN THE BUDGET

We worked hard to get Zero Fare, municipal Key Advantage, and increased resources for SEPTA into the Mayor's budget plan--help us keep up the pressure on City Council to make these wins a reality!

  1. Take City Council's city budget survey.
  2. Sign up for a hearing at City Hall
  3. Join a neighborhood budget town hall

📅 EVENTS

Apr 25

Celebrate Trails Day

Various times · Various Locations

Saturday, April 25th is Celebrate Trails Day! Throughout the city and region, there will be outdoor community events to celebrate our great network of trails.
May 14

Life After Cars Book Talk

7:00 PM, doors open 6:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S. 17th St

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
May 20

2026 Ride of Silence

6:45 PM · North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum steps

Honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets with a ride in complete silence throughout the city. The ride will cover 8 miles at a slow, casual pace and will occur rain or shine.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

Inquirer.com / Some North Philly residents are getting new homes to keep them in their ‘heavily gentrified’ neighborhoods

BPN News / Land Bank Approves 42 Housing Units at April Meeting

The Philadelphia Citizen / Will PA’s Housing Reform Plans Exclude Philly?

Inquirer.com / Villanova University, Habitat for Humanity volunteers launch Pope Leo Village housing initiative in North Philadelphia

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

The Philadelphia Citizen / Ideas We Should Steal: Fix the Sidewalks!

Inquirer.com / Thousands of abandoned cars are reported in Philly each month. Getting that number down is a challenge.

🚌 TRANSIT

Inquirer.com / Sneak peek: See inside the new Greyhound Terminal on Filbert Street

Billy Penn at WHYY / Free, year-round SEPTA passes proposed for all Philly students

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
 
Get Your Ticket Today

🕯️ RIDE OF SILENCE

Each year, Philadelphia's bicyclists come together to remember and honor those on bikes who were killed or injured by motorists with a ride around the city in complete silence. Since last year's ride, 13 bicyclists have been killed in the Delaware Valley.

This year's Ride of Silence will happen next month on May 20th. Following a brief ceremony at 6:45pm at the north apron of City Hall, participants will bike at a casual pace around the city ending at the Art Museum steps.

🚏 NEW BUS TERMINAL OPENS NEXT WEEK

Next week, the former Greyhound bus terminal will be reopening as a freshly renovated hub for Philadelphia's intercity bus passengers.

 

Check out this article from the Inquirer for a sneak peek: See inside the new Greyhound Terminal on Filbert Street

Ever since the terminal first closed years ago, we've been fighting for a facility that meets the needs of our city's bus riders so we're very excited for it to open next week!

🥳 SATURDAY: CELEBRATE TRAILS DAY

This Saturday, April 25th, is Celebrate Trails Day!

We have a great network of trails throughout the region--so let's celebrate them!

There will be outdoor community events throughout the city and region at various times throughout the day. Find an event here.

 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

BECOME A MEMBER

Jerrett Johnson of 5th Square, a transit advocacy group, urged the Council to approve a new delivery fee for nonessential products, saying the tax “will allocate funds for public transportation without impacting schools.”

Billy Penn at WHYY / Free, year-round SEPTA passes proposed for all Philly students

The passes work from 5:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. on school days, but are deactivated overnight and on weekends, holidays and over the summer. 

Transit advocate Will Tung held up his daughter’s pass during a City Hall press conference Monday and compared it to Cinderella’s carriage, which “turns into a pumpkin, useless,” at midnight.

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
